_citation: Kieffer, H. H. & Stone, T. C. (2005). The spectral irradiance of the Moon. Astronomical Journal 129, 2887-2901. DOI:10.1086/430185.
_transcription: Table 4 (p. 2896, 'ROLO Lunar Irradiance Model Coefficients, Version 311g') and Eq. 11 (p. 2897, the eight wavelength-independent constants), extracted from the PDF text by a script (the PDF's minus glyph comes out as U+0001 and was mapped to '-'). Checks: (1) read against a 200 dpi rendering of the table page; (2) Table 4 is identical to an independent transcription (github.com/mcoughlin/skybrightness data/kieffer_stone_table4.txt, sha256 bd6f9944...15aaf, retrieved 2026-09-30); (3) c1-c4 and p1-p4 are identical to those in an independent implementation (github.com/oknuutti/visnav-py visnav/calibration/moon.py, sha256 749996fc...47888); (4) the signs of the paper's Table 5 example values (p. 2897; close to, but not exactly, the band averages of Table 4) agree for every coefficient except d3, the smallest term.
_equation: Eq. 10 (p. 2895): ln A_k = sum_{i=0..3} a_ik g^i + sum_{j=1..3} b_jk Phi^(2j-1) + c1 theta + c2 phi + c3 Phi theta + c4 Phi phi + d1k exp(-g/p1) + d2k exp(-g/p2) + d3k cos[(g - p3)/p4]. A_k: disk-equivalent reflectance in band k; g: absolute phase angle; theta, phi: selenographic latitude and longitude of the observer; Phi: selenographic longitude of the Sun. Units (headings of Tables 4 and 5): g and Phi in radians in the polynomials; theta and phi in degrees; g in degrees in the exponential and cosine terms (p1-p4 in degrees). Eq. 8 (p. 2893): I_k = A_k Omega_M E_k / pi, Omega_M = 6.4177e-5 sr (the Moon at 384 400 km), E_k the solar irradiance at 1 AU; Eq. 7 scales to the actual distances.
_validity: Fitted to observations with 1.55 deg < g < 97 deg (Sec. 3.3.1, p. 2895), from the ROLO telescopes at Flagstaff (Earth-based libration range). Wavelengths are the band effective wavelengths (nm).
_table5: Table 5 (p. 2897), 'Example Lunar Irradiance Model Coefficients': [value, effect] per coefficient; 'values ... averaged over all ROLO bands ... should not be used to compute lunar albedo'; 'Effect' is 'the magnitude of the change in ln A for each term over the full range of its variables'. Used only as a check of signs and units (tests/test_rolo.py).
